questions.prompt: In a series LRC circuit, which quantity is the same through the resistor, inductor, and capacitor?
questions.answer: The same current passes through every component in a series circuit.

questions.prompt: State the impedance magnitude of a series LRC circuit.
State the phase-angle relation for a series LRC circuit.
questions.answer:
The phase angle of source voltage relative to current satisfies
\[
\tan\phi=\frac{X_L-X_C}{R}
\]

questions.prompt: A series circuit has \(R=30\,\Omega\), \(X_L=80\,\Omega\), and \(X_C=40\,\Omega\). Find \(Z\).
A series LRC circuit has \(Z=60\,\Omega\) and source voltage \(120\,\mathrm V\) rms. Find the rms current.
A series circuit has \(R=20\,\Omega\), \(X_L=70\,\Omega\), and \(X_C=45\,\Omega\). Find \(\phi\) and state whether the circuit is inductive or capacitive.
questions.answer:
\[
\tan\phi=\frac{X_L-X_C}{R}=\frac{70-45}{20}=1.25
\]
\[
\phi=51.3^\circ
\]
Since \(X_L>X_C\), the circuit is inductive and source voltage leads current.

questions.prompt: A series circuit has \(I_{\mathrm{rms}}=2.0\,\mathrm A\), \(R=10\,\Omega\), \(X_L=50\,\Omega\), and \(X_C=20\,\Omega\). Find \(V_R\), \(V_L\), and \(V_C\).
questions.answer:
Use rms component voltages:
\[
V_R=IR=(2.0)(10)=20\,\mathrm V
\]
\[
V_L=IX_L=(2.0)(50)=100\,\mathrm V
\]
\[
V_C=IX_C=(2.0)(20)=40\,\mathrm V
\]

questions.prompt: Using the circuit in the previous question, find the source rms voltage.
questions.answer:
The source voltage is the phasor sum:
\[
V=\sqrt{V_R^2+(V_L-V_C)^2}
\]
\[
V=\sqrt{20^2+(100-40)^2}=63.2\,\mathrm V
\]
This is not \(20+100+40\) because the component voltages are not in phase.

questions.prompt: A series circuit has \(R=40\,\Omega\), \(L=0.20\,\mathrm H\), \(C=50\,\mu\mathrm F\), and \(f=50\,\mathrm{Hz}\). Find \(Z\).
questions.answer:
\[
\omega=2\pi f=314\,\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}
\]
\[
X_L=\omega L=(314)(0.20)=62.8\,\Omega
\]
\[
X_C=\frac{1}{\omega C}=\frac{1}{(314)(50\times10^{-6})}=63.7\,\Omega
\]
Thus
\[
Z=\sqrt{40^2+(62.8-63.7)^2}=40.0\,\Omega
\]
The circuit is very close to resonance.

questions.prompt: Derive why the series LRC impedance uses \(X_L-X_C\), not \(X_L+X_C\).
questions.answer:
Take current as the phasor reference. The resistor voltage is in phase with current. The inductor voltage leads current by \(90^\circ\), while the capacitor voltage lags current by \(90^\circ\). Therefore the inductor and capacitor voltage phasors point in opposite vertical directions in the phasor diagram. Their net reactive voltage is
\[
I(X_L-X_C)
\]
The source voltage magnitude is therefore
\[
V=I\sqrt{R^2+(X_L-X_C)^2}
\]
so
\[
Z=\frac{V}{I}=\sqrt{R^2+(X_L-X_C)^2}
\]
